stem: Line \(k\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Line \(m\) is perpendicular to line \(k\) and passes through the point \((6, 1)\). Which equation represents line \(m\)?
solution: From the labeled points, the slope of line \(k\) is \(\frac{4 - 2}{3 - 0} = \frac{2}{3}\).
A perpendicular line has the negative reciprocal slope: \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This changes the sign of the slope of \(k\) but does not take the reciprocal.
explanation.B: Correct. The slope of \(k\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\), so line \(m\) has slope \(-\frac{3}{2}\); through \((6, 1)\), \(b = 10\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This line has the same slope as \(k\), so it is parallel to \(k\), not perpendicular.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This takes the reciprocal of the slope of \(k\) but not the opposite sign; the product of the slopes is 1, not \(-1\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
p = figure['points']
mk = Rational(p[1]['y'] - p[0]['y'], p[1]['x'] - p[0]['x'])
rhs = lambda s: value(s.split('=')[1])
ok = [k for k in choices if diff(rhs(choices[k]), x)*mk == -1 and rhs(choices[k]).subs(x, 6) == 1]
assert ok == [answer]
assert all(rhs(c).subs(x, 6) == 1 for c in choices.values())
